title: Cullen Skink
subtitle: Scottish smoked haddock and potato chowder
excerpt: Cullen skink is Scotland's most famous soup: a thick, creamy chowder of smoked haddock, leek, and potato from the fishing village of Cullen on the Moray Firth. It is hearty, deeply savoury from the smoked fish, and one of the most comforting soups in all of British cooking. It takes about 30 minutes to make.
sourceNotes: Cullen skink takes its name from the village of Cullen on the Moray Firth coast of Scotland. The word skink is an old Scottish word for a shin or knuckle -- traditionally used for a beef shin soup. Cullen skink replaces the beef with the smoked haddock for which the Moray Firth was famous. The soup is now Scotland's most internationally known recipe after haggis.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made a day ahead. Reheat gently -- do not boil.

content.text: Use undyed smoked haddock if you can find it -- the dyed yellow version is much more common, but the undyed fish has a cleaner, less aggressive flavour. Poaching the haddock in milk first creates the flavoured liquid that forms the base of the soup. Do not discard the poaching milk -- it is the heart of the chowder.

items.prepNote: white and light green parts, thinly sliced

content.text: Put {{smoked-haddock}} haddock in a wide pan. Pour {{whole-milk}} milk over. Add {{bay-leaves}} bay leaves. Bring to a bare simmer over low heat and poach for 8 minutes until the fish just flakes. Remove the fish. Strain and reserve the poaching milk. Flake the fish into large pieces, removing any skin and bones.

Melt {{unsalted-butter}} butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add {{onion}} onion and {{leek}} leek and cook for 8 minutes. Add {{potatoes-floury}} potatoes and {{fish-stock}} fish stock. Simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.

Add the reserved poaching milk and {{double-cream}} cream. Simmer gently for 5 minutes -- do not boil. Gently fold in the flaked haddock. Season with {{black-pepper}} pepper (taste before adding salt -- the smoked fish provides most of the seasoning). Scatter {{parsley-flat}} parsley over and serve with crusty bread.

items.cause: The smoked haddock has made the broth salty without adding extra salt.
items.fix: Add more unsalted milk or cream to dilute. Always taste before seasoning -- smoked fish varies considerably in salt content.

content.text: Cullen skink comes from the northeast coast of Scotland, where smoked haddock has been produced since the 17th century. The village of Cullen still holds an annual cullen skink cooking competition. The soup is on the menu of most Scottish restaurants and hotel dining rooms and is one of the dishes most closely associated with Scottish national cuisine.
